title: Gaussian-process analysis identifies active Au–Ir–Rh regions in a measured electrocatalyst library
summary: An autonomous electrochemical platform measured 966 areas across Au–Ir–Rh alloy libraries and used Gaussian-process active learning to map hydrogen-evolution activity. A noise-aware model, rerun retrospectively on the completed dataset, recovered the activity trend after 140 sampled areas and identified high-activity regions near Au30Ir20Rh50 and Au10Ir35Rh55. The approximately 15% measurement requirement is a retrospective result, and the tested library does not establish long-term catalyst stability or broader performance. This record describes the 30 May 2026 arXiv preprint; publisher-deposited metadata confirms a same-title journal version dated 20 November 2026.
ai_technology: Multi-output Gaussian-process regression and cost-aware active learning for SECCM

evidence.tested: Autonomous measurements of 966 areas supplied ground truth; a noise-aware multi-output Gaussian-process campaign was rerun retrospectively, with activity-map predictions assessed after 140 sampled areas.
evidence.unknown: Long-term catalyst stability, external replication and transfer beyond the tested alloy library and conditions are not established by the reviewed material. Final journal full text was inaccessible; its deposited abstract matches the represented result.
evidence.ai_role: Active learning guides measurement selection during autonomous electrochemical screening and predicts composition–activity trends from partial measurements; it is directly linked to finding high-activity Au–Ir–Rh compositions.

source_review.scope: Original arXiv preprint full text: active-learning operation, completed measurement campaign, retrospective noise-aware rerun, composition/activity results; arXiv version metadata and publisher-deposited journal title/abstract/authors/date.
